label: Past root compromises and coerced issuance show single-root exposure is real, not hypothetical
Observed Sybil floods in open/federated systems show plural lists without shared assurance are genuinely vulnerable
Both sides' objections being valid against distinct properties (exclusivity vs. lack of shared frame) is best explained by equivocation on "central authority"

defeaters.description: The abductive step assumes the two sides' objections are the whole of their positions. But proponents of a single no-PII root may hold a substantive (not terminological) commitment: that uniqueness guarantees require exactly one issuing authority, since any second root can mint a second identity for the same person. If so, "central authority" is not equivocated — A really does mean exclusivity, and the dispute is substantive, not a misunderstanding. The thesis's crux (2) partially concedes this.

label: Deployed transparency logs and shared assurance frameworks show each component of the hybrid already addresses the named weaknesses in analogous systems

defeaters.description: The analogy to Certificate Transparency and assurance frameworks is weakened by a disanalogy: CT and shared assurance levels work in the Web PKI because browsers act as a de facto oligopoly that enforces log policy and distrusts non-compliant CAs. Remove that enforcer and "plural roots relying parties choose among" may degrade into either no-one-checking-the-logs or a platform-bundled default list — i.e., the hybrid's Sybil and legibility guarantees may depend on precisely the kind of concentrated authority Position B rejects.

label: Once the terminological dispute is removed and the hybrid absorbs the named weaknesses, what remains contested is the three points the hybrid cannot settle by design

defeaters.description: The "only three cruxes remain" claim omits at least one further genuine disagreement: revocation semantics and interoperability of revocation across roots. If a credential is portable across roots but revocation is per-root, a person excluded by one root can continue presenting a credential anchored elsewhere — which Position A would regard as the Sybil problem reappearing, and Position B would regard as the appeal mechanism working. This is not reducible to cruxes (1)–(3) and suggests the residual set is larger than claimed.

label: If the dispute is partly equivocation, the hybrid satisfies both sides' core requirements, and only three cruxes remain, then the thesis holds
